attempts.raw_response: The statement came amid heated debate over the proposed Sizewell C nuclear plant, with local residents and environmental groups raising serious concerns about increased traffic during construction. Transport experts warned that the additional heavy goods vehicles would cause significant disruption to existing road networks, particularly along the A12 corridor which already handles substantial commuter traffic. Norfolk County Council echoed these reservations, emphasising that any approval would require substantial improvements to local infrastructure. Meanwhile, campaigners from Stop Sizewell C argued that the promised economic benefits would be outweighed by environmental damage to nearby wildlife habitats and the Suffolk coast. The consultation period remains open until next month, with final decisions expected from the Planning Inspectorate later this year.
